Notation of mhpfilter

Source: R/common-notation.R
mhp_notation.Rd

The symbols used in the help pages and vignettes of mhpfilter, with their meaning and the argument or result component that holds them. The notation follows one rule throughout: scalars are upper-case letters in normal face (\(P\), \(R\)), indices lower-case italic (\(i, j\)), vectors lower-case bold (\(\mathbf{y}\), \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\)) and matrices upper-case bold (\(\mathbf{X}\), \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\)).

Usage

mhp_notation(format = c("table", "path", "tex"))

Arguments

format

"table" (default: a data.table with columns symbol (LaTeX), text (plain text), kind (scalar, index, vector, matrix, set, function, operator), meaning and argument), "path" (the path of notation.csv) or "tex" (the path of Notations.tex, the notation appendix used in the articles).

Value

See format.

See also

Other mhpfilter utilities: mhp_reference(), mhp_save(), mhp_theme()

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

mhp_notation(
    format = c("table", "path", "tex")[1]
  )
#>                                    symbol            text   kind
#>                                    <char>          <char> <char>
#>  1:                                     T               T scalar
#>  2:                                  t, j             t j  index
#>  3:                           \\mathbf{x}               x vector
#>  4:                           \\mathbf{g}               g vector
#>  5:                           \\mathbf{c}               c vector
#>  6:                           \\mathbf{K}               K matrix
#>  7:                           \\mathbf{A}               A matrix
#>  8:                           \\mathbf{I}               I matrix
#>  9:                           \\mathbf{B}               B matrix
#> 10:                              \\lambda          lambda scalar
#> 11:                            \\lambda_t        lambda_t vector
#> 12:                               \\alpha           alpha scalar
#> 13:                                     k               k scalar
#> 14:                               \\omega           omega scalar
#> 15:                          P_t(\\omega)      P_t(omega) scalar
#> 16:                               l(t), L          l(t) L scalar
#> 17:                               \\theta           theta scalar
#> 18:                                \\mu_i            mu_i scalar
#> 19:                      \\phi_1, \\phi_2     phi_1 phi_2 scalar
#> 20: \\sigma_\\varepsilon, \\sigma_\\delta sigma_e sigma_d scalar

#>  6:                         (T - 2) x T matrix of second differences

#>  9:  smoother: g = B x; row t holds the weights of the estimate at t
#> 10:                                              smoothing parameter

#> 15:                                        gain of the estimate at t

#> 17:                     spacing of the frequencies in the loss (0.1)
#> 18:                                     eigenvalues of A (exact GCV)
#> 19:                          AR(2) coefficients of a simulated cycle
#> 20:                standard deviations of the trend and cycle shocks
